raw_text:
Below is a 12‑week general fitness programme tailored for a 58‑year‑old male, 6 months post‑MI, cleared for moderate‑intensity exercise only. Key safety rules to follow every session:
- Keep HR < ~115 bpm (70% age‑predicted max). If client is on HR‑modifying meds (β‑blocker), HR will be unreliable — use RPE (Borg 6–20 ≈ 11–13) and the talk test instead.  
- No Valsalva: cue to inhale on the easier (eccentric) phase and exhale during exertion (concentric). Avoid breath‑holding.  
- No maximal lifts, no heavy loads. Use machines, cables, bodyweight and light free weights. Controlled tempo.  
- Stop and seek medical review for chest pain, sudden severe shortness of breath, syncope, dizziness or unusual palpitations.  
- Measure resting BP and HR before exercise; if abnormal per his medical team, delay session.

Programme overview
- Frequency: 4 sessions/week (2 supervised resistance sessions + 2 cardio/endurance sessions) + 1 optional light active recovery/mobility day. Rest days between heavier sessions.  
- Phases: Phase 1 (weeks 1–4) — adaptation and safety; Phase 2 (weeks 5–8) — steady progression of volume; Phase 3 (weeks 9–12) — consolidation and modest capacity increase.  
- Intensity: Moderate (RPE 11–13 / talk test comfortable conversation). HR cap <115 bpm.  
- Strength goals: muscular endurance, posture, balance, functional strength. 2–3 sets, 8–15 reps, controlled tempo.  
- Cardio goals: build aerobic base. Continuous steady state with brief low‑grade intervals only if HR remains safe.

General session structure (all sessions)
1. Pre‑exercise check: symptoms, resting BP and HR if available.  
2. Warm‑up 8–12 min: light cardio (walking/recumbent bike/elliptical) 6–8 min + mobility (shoulder circles, leg swings, hip hinges, ankle mobility) 2–4 min. Keep HR well below cap.  
3. Main set: see session plans below. Monitor HR & RPE continuously.  
4. Cool‑down 6–10 min: easy cardio 4–6 min bringing HR down + static stretches 4–6 min (hamstrings, quads, calves, chest, shoulders).  
5. Breathing cue: exhale on exertion, inhale on return.

Progression strategy
- Progress by adding time (cardio +5–10 min), adding 1 set, or increasing reps within safe RPE band before increasing load. Increase load only when client can complete target reps with RPE ≤ 12 and HR well below 115. Small increases (5–10%) only.  
- Track symptoms and HR response; if HR approaches cap consistently, allow more recovery or reduce intensity.

Weekly schedule (useable template)
- Day 1: Strength Session A (full body)  
- Day 2: Cardio steady state (moderate)  
- Day 3: Rest or mobility/yoga (optional active recovery)  
- Day 4: Strength Session B (full body + balance/core)  
- Day 5: Cardio steady state (or machine cross‑training)  
- Days 6–7: 1 rest day + optional light walk or mobility

Detailed 12‑week plan

PHASE 1 — Weeks 1–4: Adaptation, technique, baseline conditioning
Goal: Safe reintroduction; improve mobility, build 2–3 sessions/week habit.

Weeks 1–2 (foundation)
Strength A (Day 1) — machines / bodyweight, tempo 2‑0‑2
- Leg press (or sit‑to‑stand from bench) — 2 sets x 12 reps, rest 60–90s  
- Seated row (machine or cable) — 2 x 12, 60s rest  
- Chest press (machine) — 2 x 12, 60s rest  
- Seated leg curl or supported hamstring curl — 2 x 12, 60s  
- Seated overhead press (light DB or machine) — 2 x 10, 60–90s  
- Standing calf raise (machine or bodyweight) — 2 x 12–15  
- Core: Deadbug (floor) — 2 x 8–10 per side (slow)  
Warm‑up & cool‑down as above.

Cardio (Day 2) — choose treadmill walking, stationary bike, or elliptical
- 20–25 minutes continuous at moderate intensity (RPE 11–12). Maintain HR well below 115. If HR creeps up, reduce pace or incline.  
- Add 2 x 30–60s small pick‑ups (slightly faster pace) only if HR <100 during steady state. Otherwise keep steady.

Strength B (Day 4)
- Step‑ups to low box or small step — 2 x 10 per leg  
- Lat pulldown (or assisted pull) — 2 x 12  
- Hip bridge — 2 x 12  
- Cable or machine chest fly (light) — 2 x 12  
- Seated single‑arm row (light) — 2 x 10 each side  
- Single‑leg balance to stable hold (eyes open) — 3 x 20–30s per leg  
- Plank on knees (or full if comfortable) — 2 x 20–30s

Cardio (Day 5)
- 20–25 minutes low impact cross‑training (recumbent bike or rower light), RPE 11–12.

Weeks 3–4 (build slightly)
- Strength sessions: progress to 2–3 sets x 10–12 reps; add 5–10% load if RPE ≤ 12 and HR response safe. Keep rest 60–90s. Add 1 extra core exercise (bird‑dog 2 x 8–10).  
- Cardio: increase to 25–30 minutes steady state. Optional 3 x 30s gentle pick‑ups if HR remains under limit; otherwise keep even pace.  
- Introduce light interval format only as 30s gentle faster / 90s easy for 4–6 cycles if tolerated and HR <115.

PHASE 2 — Weeks 5–8: Build volume & functional strength
Goal: Increase time and volume, add more functional movements and balance challenge.

Weeks 5–6
Strength A (Day 1) — 3 sets where tolerated
- Leg press or goblet squat (use light DB, controlled) — 3 x 10–12  
- Seated row (or TRX rows if stable) — 3 x 10–12  
- Chest press machine (light) — 3 x 10–12  
- Romanian deadlift with DB (light) or hip hinge on cable — 3 x 10 (focus on hamstring control)  
- Seated overhead press (DB or machine) — 3 x 8–10  
- Farmer carry (light DBs, 30–45s) OR walking with light load — 2 x 30–45s (good for posture and functional cardio)  
- Core: Deadbug + plank (2 x each)

Cardio (Day 2)
- 30–35 minutes steady state at RPE 11–13. Options: treadmill incline walking (low incline), stationary bike, elliptical. Monitor HR. Keep longer warm‑up/cool‑down.

Strength B (Day 4)
- Split squat (rear foot elevated or static lunge, with support if needed) — 3 x 8–10 per leg  
- Lat pulldown or machine pulldown — 3 x 10–12  
- Cable chest press or pec deck (light) — 3 x 10–12  
- Seated leg curl — 3 x 12  
- Standing single‑leg RDL to box (balance + hamstring) — 2 x 8 each side  
- Core: Pallof press (anti‑rotation cable) — 3 x 8–10 per side  
- Balance: tandem walk or single leg hold 2 x 30s

Cardio (Day 5)
- 30–35 minutes cross‑training. Introduce interval option 4–6 cycles of 60s slightly higher pace / 120s easy, only if HR stays <115. If on beta‑blocker use RPE instead.

Weeks 7–8
- Strength: maintain 3 sets, increase reps to 12–15 on some accessory moves for endurance (e.g., calf raises, single‑leg balance). Slightly increase load on compound machine moves if safe. Keep tempo controlled.  
- Cardio: progress to 35–40 minutes steady state. Keep HR <115; use brief 1:3 intervals if desired (e.g., 60s stronger / 180s easy) and HR safe.  
- Add a supervised circuit once per week if client tolerates: 6 stations, low load, 45s work / 60–90s rest, 2 rounds (monitor HR closely).

PHASE 3 — Weeks 9–12: Consolidation and modest capacity increase
Goal: Improve functional strength, endurance and confidence while maintaining cardiac safety.

Weeks 9–10
Strength A (Day 1) — full body emphasis on functional strength
- Leg press or goblet squat — 3 x 8–12 (choose weight to keep RPE ≤ 13)  
- Seated row or TRX row with added reps — 3 x 10–12  
- Incline chest press (machine or DB) light — 3 x 8–10  
- Romanian deadlift (light DBs) — 3 x 8–10  
- Overhead press (machine or seated DB) — 3 x 8–10  
- Farmer carry or suitcase carry — 2 x 45–60s (light)  
- Core: plank 3 x 30s, deadbug 3 x 10/side

Cardio (Day 2)
- 35–45 minutes steady state at RPE 11–13. Consider mixing modalities (bike + treadmill) to reduce joint load. Add short purposeful hills on treadmill (low incline, keep HR safe).

Strength B (Day 4)
- Step up + balance (higher step if safe) — 3 x 8–10 per leg  
- Lat pulldown / assisted pull — 3 x 8–12  
- Cable chest press + single arm rows superset (light) — 3 x 10 each  
- Glute bridge march or single leg bridge — 3 x 10  
- Unilateral RDL — 3 x 8–10 each leg  
- Core: Pallof press 3 x 10/side, bird‑dog 3 x 8–10/side

Cardio (Day 5)
- 35–45 minutes cross‑training. Option: two 12–15 minute blocks on different machines (bike + rower) for variety.

Weeks 11–12
- Strength: maintain 3 sets. If well tolerated and heart response stable, increase reps or add one heavier set for compound machine moves but keep RPE ≤ 13. More focus on multi‑joint movement quality and balance.  
- Cardio: keep 40–45 minutes steady state most sessions. You can include one session with 4–6 short pick‑ups (60s) but only if HR remains comfortably below limit and RPE still moderate.  
- Final week: review progress, functional tests (sit‑to‑stand, 6‑minute walk test) only if cleared and with cardiac precautions.

Example session details and exercise notes
- Load guidance: no 1RM testing. Use perceived exertion: pick a weight that feels like 11–13 on Borg (somewhat hard but sustainable for the set).  
- Sets/reps: typical pattern across phases: begin 2 sets x 12 → progress to 3 sets x 8–12 or 12–15 for endurance moves.  
- Rest: 60–120s between compound sets; 30–60s between accessory sets.  
- Tempo: controlled (2 s descent, 1 s pause if needed, 1–2 s concentric) — no explosive lifts.  
- Breathing: exhale through concentric, inhale on eccentric. Cue client frequently to avoid breath‑holding.

Sample exercises bank (use across weeks)
- Lower: Leg press, goblet squat (light), step‑ups, split squat, seated leg curl, Romanian deadlift with DB, calf raises, glute bridges.  
- Upper: Seated row, lat pulldown, chest press (machine), cable chest press/flies, seated overhead press (machine/DB), single‑arm cable row.  
- Core/Balance: Deadbug, bird‑dog, Pallof press, plank (knee or full), single‑leg balance, tandem walk.  
- Cardio machines: treadmill (walk), stationary bike, recumbent bike, elliptical, rower (light).

Monitoring and safety specifics
- HR: use chest strap or wrist monitor. Stop if HR approaches 115 bpm; reduce intensity or rest. If on β‑blocker rely on RPE.  
- BP: if pre‑exercise systolic BP >160 mmHg or diastolic >100 mmHg (or per his cardiologist limits), avoid exercise and contact provider. Trainer should follow clinic protocol.  
- Symptoms: chest pain, unusual SOB, dizziness, palpitations → stop and seek medical attention.  
- Valsalva: coach continuous rhythmic breathing. For heavier lifts, avoid breath‑holding altogether.

Nutrition & recovery guidance (cardiac focused)
- Dietary pattern: recommend Mediterranean / DASH style — plenty of vegetables, fruit, whole grains, lean proteins (fish, poultry, legumes), nuts, seeds, olive oil. Limit saturated fats, processed foods, added sugars, and high sodium.  
- Protein: aim ~1.0–1.2 g/kg/day distributed across meals to support muscle maintenance (adjust per body composition goals and renal function).  
- Hydration: adequate fluid intake; avoid large meals immediately before exercise.  
- Alcohol: moderate or as advised by cardiologist.  
- Supplements: follow physician guidance (e.g., statins or other meds may be prescribed). Avoid starting new supplements without medical clearance.  
- Sleep & recovery: aim for 7–9 hours/night. Schedule 48 hours between tougher strength sessions if muscle soreness present. Use foam rolling and mobility on rest days.

Additional trainer notes
- Start every client session with symptom & medication review. Know his current meds. If on nitrates or sublingual nitroglycerin, ensure it's accessible.  
- Keep sessions supervised for first 6–8 weeks; progress only when vitals and symptoms stable.  
- Document resting and peak HR during sessions and any symptoms. Communicate with the client’s cardiology/cardiac rehab team if irregular responses occur.  
- If the client wants to progress beyond this 12‑week plan (higher intensity or interval training), require written clearance from cardiology and a graded exercise test.

If you want, I can:
- Convert this into an easy‑to‑print weekly template for the client,  
- Provide suggested progression percentages for specific machine loads, or  
- Adapt the plan for a 3‑day/week schedule or home‑based training. Which would you prefer?
